reasons.correctness_risk: Generates pseudo-legal moves on a 0x88 board, then keeps only those that leave the king safe. Castling out of, through and into check, the en-passant victim and pin checks, castling rights and both counters all read correct, and perft to depth 3 on three standard positions backs this up.
reasons.structure: Small single-purpose functions, plus a lazy legal-move generator that lets status and applyMove stop early. Castling legality is split between addCastles and the legality filter, and e1/e8 appear as bare indices 4 and 116.
reasons.readability: Clear names, JSDoc on the public API, named home, promotion and en-passant ranks, and a comment explaining 0x88. The rights update is easy to follow, though the 0x88 step offsets assume chess-programming background.
reasons.error_handling: Rejects a non-string FEN with a TypeError and validates every FEN field, the rank widths, and missing or duplicate kings. It screens the move string before searching, and the tests check error paths by message.
reasons.tests: Exact-FEN checks for the counters (including values beyond 2^53), all four castles, castling safety (with a Black through-check case), rights after king moves, rook moves and corner captures, en passant (expiry, missing victim, rank pin), every promotion for both colours, both mates, check and stalemate. Also perft to depth 3 on the start position, Kiwipete and position 3, and timing assertions for both stated performance limits.

reasons.correctness_risk: Same sound design (row/file board, legality by making the move and testing king safety, castling transit check, corner rights checked by colour) and no rule defect found. Assurance is lower because move generation is pinned only to perft depth 2 on two positions.
reasons.structure: Well-factored helpers, named CASTLING and CORNERS tables, and rights logic isolated in remainingRights. Castling safety is a special-case branch inside isLegal.
reasons.readability: Row/file arithmetic is intuitive and the names are good. But remainingRights packs four conditions with optional chaining into one filter, comments are sparse, and the tests misspell Kiwipete as KIWIPIETE.
reasons.error_handling: Validates FEN fields, ranks, widths and that both kings are present, and rejects non-string moves without coercing them. A non-string FEN fails only by accident (a TypeError from trim), a FEN with two kings is accepted and only the first is guarded, and no FEN error path is tested.
reasons.tests: Good targeted cases (castling safety, corner-capture rights, en passant including check evasion and the rank pin, promotions, both mates, stalemate) and perft depth 2 for the start position and Kiwipete. But there are no timing checks for the stated limits and no invalid-FEN tests, castling safety is tested for White only, and the subprocess and coercion-hook tests pin behaviour the request does not ask for.

why: Both engines share the same sound design and I found no rule defect in either, so the difference is in validation and verification. X pins its move generator with perft to depth 3 on three standard positions, asserts both stated performance limits, and validates FEN input more strictly, with tests. Y stops at perft depth 2, never checks the performance requirements, and spends test effort on coercion and subprocess behaviour the request does not ask for.
